text:
tara: Quick note from the lark-int4 onboarding slice: funcall JSON failures rose from 0.2% -> 1.7% after the latest quant pass. Failures concentrated on very short outputs (single key-value args).

ben: yikes. any minimal examples?

tara: pasted minimal failing sample: 
int4: {"command":"set_topic","args":{"topic":"you’re up"}}
parser: Error: Invalid escape at pos 13

fp16: {"command":"set_topic","args":{"topic":"you're up"}}

olga: same class as the smart-apostrophe/escape issues we've seen. But also some traces of duplicated escapes (\\n) in a subset.

canary-bot: Alert: lark-int4 structured_parse_fail_rate=1.7% (baseline=0.2%) on suite/funcall-short.

ben: immediate mitigations?

tara: propose two parallel actions: (A) quick parser-level normalizer to map curly quotes -> ASCII, collapse double backslashes, and NFKC normalize; (B) schedule an int4 token-bias rebuild that slightly penalizes punctuation tokens at chunk tails to reduce stray commas/apostrophes.

olga: for (A) we must not hide raw failure signals. Telemetry labels: raw_fail, normalized_repair, final_parse_success. Gate decisions should still consider raw_fail.

ben: also consider adaptive fp16 fallback: if a request fails strict parse after one deterministic sanitizer attempt, re-run on fp16 and surface both outputs in logs. Rate-cap fallbacks to 0.5% to control cost.

tara: implemented a lightweight normalizer prototype locally: recovers ~70% of recent failures. I'll open a tiny PR behind a feature flag with metrics in 30m.

olga: good. For (B) I'll spin a small canary build with token-bias tweak (job id bias-run-173456-1). ETA ~25m. We'll compare token sequences on failing examples to see which subtokens toggle.

canary-bot: Update: bias-run-173456-1 completed. raw_parse_fail_rate int4 -> 1.6% (no significant change). Token-diff logs uploaded to /canaries/lark/bias-run-173456-1/diffs.tar.gz.

ben: hmm bias tweak didn't help much. That points to quant-induced stochasticity in fine-grained subtokens rather than a single punctuation token bias.

olga: agree. Longer-term: we may need a quant-aware tokenizer remap or retrain with tokenization stability objective. Short-term: ship normalizer to Hosted behind a flag and enable adaptive-fallback for Dedicated customers at lower rate.

tara: PR #4278 opened: parser-normalizer + telemetry. Demo shows repaired percentage ~70% and preserves raw_fail metric.

ben: add a small targeted golden set (contractions, diacritics, emoji-only, multi-byte punctuation) to the onboarding canary so future regressions are gated earlier. Also add a daily summary comparing int4 vs fp16 on the short-output slice.

olga: agreed. Ill add token-boundary logging for samples that still fail after normalization so we can triage which subtokens flip under int4.

canary-bot: Reminder: feature-flagged normalizer will auto-disable after 48h unless manually extended.

tara: thanks all. follow-up: if normalized_repair <50% after 24h, we'll roll back the int4 cohort and open a deeper investigation with the quantization team.

ben: sounds good. tagging quant-team for visibility.

olga: I'll post diffs and token logs to the thread when ready.

tara: demo scheduled for tomorrow 10:30am. :coffee:
